# Built-in plugins

LYNX ships its own native instruments and effects: engines inspired by the classic third-party plugins, LYNX
originals, and clean-room re-implementations of the FL Studio natives.

<!-- inspired:begin (generated by scripts/gen-inspired.py) -->
## Inspired by the classics

LYNX ships **native** plugins inspired by the third-party plugins producers use most, next to its clean-room FL Studio natives. 24 dedicated LYNX engines are in, more are being built, and a project that uses one of the 56 originals below **opens with the LYNX equivalent** when the original is not installed (its settings are kept and come back once it is; see [PLUGIN_FALLBACK.md](PLUGIN_FALLBACK.md)).

## FL Studio natives

Most of LYNX's built-in engines are **clean-room re-implementations of the
native plugins of FL Studio**, written from scratch after a behavioural study of each plugin (decompilation
studied, the official manual and project data, then LYNX's engine checked against the original plugin running
unmodified in a test harness). How each one was decoded is documented round by round in
[`docs/analise/`](analise/); the full technical status is in [`docs/STATUS.md`](STATUS.md).

FL Studio's plugin names are used below only to say which plugin each LYNX engine is compatible with or inspired
by. No Image-Line code, audio or wave data is part of LYNX: where an engine needs a plugin's built-in waves,
samples, impulses or tables, LYNX reads them at run time from **your own** FL Studio installation (marked †).

## Featured

The plugins FL Studio users reach for most, all shipping in LYNX at **Exact** or **Near-exact** quality, plus LYNX's
own reverbs fitted to black-box measurements of the third-party reverbs producers use most (see
[LYNX originals: reverbs](#lynx-originals-reverbs)). (Sytrus and Harmor are not featured yet: both are *Close* — see
[Generators](#generators).)

## Status legend

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Exact** | bit-identical to the original plugin's output on every state found in an FL Studio installation (demo projects and presets) and on synthetic tests |
| **Near-exact** | bit-identical on most states; the rest differ below about −100 dB (last-bit rounding of the original's math library) — inaudible |
| **Close** | the same algorithm; within −60 dB of the original on (almost) all tested states, typically −80 dB or better; the gaps are listed |
| **Approximate** | the plugin's saved settings are mapped onto a LYNX built-in effect or synth: similar sound, not the same engine |
| **Placeholder** | the state is kept and the plugin makes no sound / passes audio through, as the original does in FL Studio 2026 |
| **Fitted** | LYNX's own engine (not the original's algorithm), designed so that black-box measurements of the third-party original — decay times per band, onset, build-up, levels, filters, parameter laws — match within the tolerances listed for it |

**How you get it:** *Insert* = can be added to any mixer insert (Mixer slot menu or the F8 quick-add palette).
*Import* = created when you open an FL Studio project (`.flp`) or drop an FL effect preset; the engine is kept
in the `.lynx` project and its controls stay editable and automatable. *Substitute* = also stands in automatically for
the third-party plugin when a project uses it and it is not installed ([`PLUGIN_FALLBACK.md`](PLUGIN_FALLBACK.md)): its
saved settings are translated and the original stays in the project byte for byte.

| Fruity Phaser | Fruity Phaser | Insert | Exact | all 27 presets at 44.1–96 kHz bit-identical (round 105) |
| Fruity 7 Band EQ | Fruity 7 Band EQ | Insert | Exact | all 13 installation states and 40 random ones with control changes at 22.05–96 kHz bit-identical; designed at 44.1 kHz whatever the rate, as FL (round 165k) |
| Fruity Bass Boost | Fruity Bass Boost | Insert | Exact | all 3 installation states and 40 random ones at 22.05–96 kHz bit-identical (round 165k) |
| Fruity Delay (v1) | Fruity Delay | Insert | Exact | all 7 installation states and 40 random ones (three modes, host / fixed tempo, control changes, 1–512-frame calls) at 22.05–96 kHz bit-identical; Tempo = host follows the song tempo (round 165k) |
| Fruity Center | Fruity Center | Insert | Exact | bit-identical at 22.05–96 kHz (round 165k) |
| Fruity Phase Inverter | Fruity Phase Inverter | Insert | Exact | bit-identical; FL's default inverts the right side only (round 165k) |
| Gross Beat | Gross Beat | Import | Exact | all 41 states; MIDI control of the slots and spline curves missing |
| Squeeze | Fruity Squeeze | Import | Near-exact | within 5·10⁻⁹ of the reference model, which is bit-exact with FL |
| Effector | Effector | Insert | Near-exact | all 12 algorithms; reverb −100 dB |
| Maximus † | Maximus | Import | Near-exact | 96/100 demo states within −139 dB; v15 linear-phase split and Master Mid keep an approximation |
| Soundgoodizer † | Soundgoodizer | Import | Near-exact | within −126 dB on every preset/amount |
| Convolver † | Fruity Convolver | Import | Near-exact | −127…−152 dB; states with a shaped EQ curve are approximated |
| Distructor † | Distructor | Import | Near-exact | bit-identical except the Harmor shapes and the cabinet |
| Vocodex † | Vocodex | Import | Near-exact | −136…−145 dB (internal Sytrus carrier −112 dB) |
| Vintage Phaser | Vintage Phaser | Import | Near-exact | within −121 dB |
| Pitch correction | Pitcher | Insert | Close | bit-exact with the reference model; MIDI mode / Harmonize get no MIDI in LYNX |
| Newtone | Newtone | Import | Close | pass-through as FL; in slave mode the note edits (pitch offsets and transitions, drift, vibrato, tremolo, ramps, formant, volume, timing, disabled notes) rendered by LYNX's own pitch engine: against FL's own engine on 135 states every note's level within 0.4 dB and its median pitch within 9 cents, unedited notes bit-identical; legato glides with long smooth times (up to 40 c) and FL's sample re-alignment after edits differ (round 165g) |
| Newtime | Newtime | Import | Placeholder | pass-through (as FL) + the source sample in slave mode; time warping not reproduced |
| Utility | Transporter | Insert | Approximate | mapped to a utility stage |
| Limiter | Emphasis | Insert | Approximate | not ported yet |

**Windows.** Every native effect opens its own window (double-click its Mixer slot, or the **Editor** button over its
knobs). For the plugins studied so far — Fruity Limiter, Parametric EQ 2, Delay 3, Multiband Compressor, Reeverb 2,
LuxeVerb, Compressor, Filter, Fast Dist, Chorus, Flanger, Stereo Enhancer, Gross Beat, Delay 2, Reeverb, Flangus, Soft
Clipper, Blood Overdrive, PanOMatic, Stereo Shaper, Transient Processor, Free Filter, WaveShaper, Vintage Chorus, Hyper
Chorus, Balance, Squeeze, Soundgoodizer, and the 3x Osc, FL Keys, BooBass, Sytrus (main page) and Harmor pages
of the channel settings — the window has the same controls, sections, captions and arrangement as the FL plugin,
drawn in LYNX's own style, with a presets bar that lists the plugin's FL presets from your installation
([`docs/analise/UI_STUDY_plugins93.md`](analise/UI_STUDY_plugins93.md)); the other effects show their controls as a
grid of knobs.

Also on every insert: LYNX's own Filter, Distortion, Lo-fi, Reverb, Compressor, Limiter, Crossover, Volume gate,
Rhythmic envelope, Auto-pan and the **Patcher** (round 141): a node graph of effects, instruments and VST3/CLAP plugins
with audio, note and control cables, delay-compensated like FL's — as a mixer slot or a Channel Rack generator, with
extra outputs to other inserts; FL projects' Patchers open as the same graph. Plus any VST3/CLAP plugin. FL's Peak, Envelope and Keyboard Controllers are imported
as LYNX controllers.

## LYNX originals: the mixing suite

Five effects of LYNX's own design for vocal and mix chains (REA round 96, [`docs/analise/REA_rodada96.md`](analise/REA_rodada96.md)).
They are **not** models or copies of any product: each fills the *role* of a familiar kind of studio processor and
is written only from published DSP knowledge (textbooks, AES / DAFx papers and public circuit analyses of classic
hardware). No third-party plugin was opened, run or analysed to make them, and no preset, name, graphic or manual
text of one is used. All are on every mixer insert (*Insert*), report their latency before the first block, have their own panels with live gain-reduction meters,
oversample where they are nonlinear and never allocate on the audio thread.

| LYNX engine | In the role of | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Ridge Strip | console channel strips, e.g. SSL E-series channels (Waves SSL E-Channel, SSL Native 4K E) | 18 dB/oct high-pass, 12 dB/oct low-pass, four bands with two curve families (brown: constant Q, plain shelves; black: proportional Q, shelves with the overshoot dip), compressor (soft knee, fast attack, release, parallel mix), gate / 1:2 expander, EQ ↔ dynamics order, filters to the sidechain, phase, input / output trims, gain-reduction meters |
| Glow Leveler | optical levelers such as the Teletronix LA-2A (Waves CLA-2A, UA LA-2A) | feedback leveler with an electro-optical cell model: ~10 ms attack, two-stage release that lengthens after long or heavy leveling; peak reduction, gain, compress / limit, sidechain emphasis, mix |
| Hush De-esser | de-essers (Waves DeEsser, FabFilter Pro-DS) | split-band (complementary crossover) or wideband reduction, high-pass or band detector, frequency, threshold, range, release, listen, 2 ms lookahead |
| Aether | "air" EQs and high-frequency exciters (Slate Digital Fresh Air, Maag EQ4 air band) | broad high shelf up to +15 dB (5–20 kHz) plus a 4x-oversampled harmonic exciter on the band above its frequency, even ↔ odd character, mix |
| Quell Denoiser | one-knob noise suppressors (Waves NS1) | six-band Linkwitz-Riley split with all-pass compensation, a soft-knee downward expander per band whose threshold, depth and trim follow Amount, fast opening and a slower close, linked stereo, listen, output |
| Gemini Doubler | doublers (Waves Doubler) | two voices, each a pitch-shifting delay (two crossfaded grains): gain, equal-power pan, delay, feedback with a low cut, detune, triangle LFO on the pitch, octave down, source L / sum / difference; the direct signal rotated in the stereo field and aligned with the voices; first-order voice shelves |
| Ember Saturator | analog saturators (Soundtoys Decapitator, FabFilter Saturn) | tube (asymmetric, even harmonics), tape (pre/de-emphasis, odd), transistor and fuzz curves; drive, tone tilt, low / high cut, auto gain, mix, 2x / 4x / 8x oversampling with a constant latency; since round 108 a multiband mode: up to four Linkwitz-Riley bands (12 / 24 / 48 dB/oct, summing flat) with their own style, drive, mix and level |

Product names in the table are trademarks of their owners (Solid State Logic, Waves Audio, Universal Audio,
FabFilter, Slate Digital, Maag Audio, Soundtoys and the owners of the Teletronix name); they are used only to say
which role each LYNX effect plays. LYNX is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by any of them.

## LYNX originals: reverbs

Six reverbs of LYNX's own design (REA round 100, [`docs/analise/REA_rodada100.md`](analise/REA_rodada100.md)), each
**inspired by** a Valhalla DSP reverb and fitted to measurements of it. The originals were only hosted the way a DAW
hosts them — the official demo versions, VST3 parameter API, test signals in, audio out — never opened, decompiled or
disassembled; no preset, graphic or manual text was copied. The DSP is LYNX's own, written from the published
literature (Schroeder / Moorer all-pass diffusion, Jot's feedback delay networks with frequency-dependent absorption,
Dattorro's input diffusers, a two-head delay-line pitch shifter). The parameter laws follow the measured ones, so a
project's saved Valhalla settings translate one to one when LYNX stands in for a missing Valhalla plugin; the effects
also sit on any mixer insert (*Insert*), have their own panels, no latency, and never allocate on the audio thread.

| LYNX engine | Inspired by | What it is | Fit (48 kHz, impulse responses) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Epoch Verb | ValhallaVintageVerb | 22 algorithms (halls, plates, rooms, chambers, chorused / random spaces, gated, drifting …), 1970s / 1980s / Now colour, pre-delay, decay 0.2–70 s, size, attack, bass multiply / crossover, high shelf, early / late diffusion, modulation, high / low cut, equal-power mix | mid-band RT60 within ±8 % on 22 modes and 0.5–8 s decays; onsets within 1 ms; energy of the first 100 ms within ±2 dB on most modes |
| Atrium | ValhallaRoom | 12 room / chamber / space types; early section (size, cross, modulation, send into the late part) and late section (size, cross, modulation); bass and high RT multipliers with crossovers; space; high / low cut | RT60 = Decay within ±10 % (0.5–8 s) per octave band 125 Hz–4 kHz |
| Foil Plate | ValhallaPlate | 12 plate types, pre-delay, decay 0.5–30 s, size, width, modulation, low / high EQ shelves | RT60 at low / mid frequencies = Decay; the measured high-frequency damping that grows with decay |
| Nebula | Valhalla Supermassive | delay 0–2000 ms or synced (note / dotted / triplet), feedback (√F per pass, as measured), density, warp, width, low / high cut, modulation, 22 network shapes | echo spacing and decay per shape as measured (Delay × shape multiple, decay multiple at density 0 and 100 %) |
| Halo | ValhallaShimmer | shimmer: −12…+12 semitone shifter in the feedback path (single / dual voices, or off), size-set decay, diffusion, colour, low / high cut, modulation | shift law and size → decay law as measured; the mode lists are partly not confirmed |
| Horizon | ValhallaFutureVerb | echo (12 modes: clean, tape, digital, analog, detune, reverse and reverse-octave, sparkle, swarm, lo-fi; time / sync, feedback, spread, drive, detune) into or after a reverb (8 modes, decay 0.2–70 s, size, attack, early / late, density), colour, low / high EQ, width | reverb decay per mode as measured; the echo modes are our own interpretation |

Valhalla, ValhallaVintageVerb, ValhallaRoom, ValhallaPlate, Supermassive, ValhallaShimmer and ValhallaFutureVerb are
trademarks of Valhalla DSP, LLC; they are named only to say which plugin each LYNX reverb is inspired by and stands in
for. LYNX is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Valhalla DSP.

## LYNX originals: delay and modulation

Four effects of LYNX's own design (REA round 101, [`docs/analise/REA_rodada101.md`](analise/REA_rodada101.md)),
inspired by the delay / modulation plugins producers use most. They are written from published DSP literature
(fractional delay lines, the Hilbert-transform frequency shifter, delay-line pitch shifting, barber-pole and
through-zero flanging, tape and bucket-brigade echo descriptions from AES / DAFx papers and textbooks). The
reference plugins — the official demos, installed by the user — were only **measured from the outside**, the way a
DAW hosts them (parameter names and value laws, test signals in, audio out); nothing in them was decompiled or
copied. Their parameters follow the measured value laws, so when a project uses one of the originals on a machine
that does not have it, the LYNX effect stands in **with the saved settings translated** (the original's state stays in
the project byte for byte and is used again once the plugin is installed — see [`PLUGIN_FALLBACK.md`](PLUGIN_FALLBACK.md)).

| LYNX engine | Inspired by | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Echoform | ValhallaDelay | 12 characters: tape (head bump, roll-off that falls with the delay time, wow / flutter, saturation), hi-fi tape, bucket brigade (1.6 kHz, noise with age), analog (3.4 kHz), digital (8 kHz, age = bit / rate reduction), clean (age = low-pass), frequency shifter (every repeat moves by the shift), pitch (±24 st, L / R detune), reverse, lo-fi, phaser, detune; single / dual / ratio / ping-pong / quad styles; ms or tempo sync (straight, dotted, triplet); feedback to 200 % (bounded); diffusion; low / high cut; LFO; ducking; width; equal-power mix |
| Spiral Echo | ValhallaFreqEcho | frequency-shifting echo: shift ±1 kHz added on every repeat (in stereo the right side hears each repeat with the opposite shift), 0.01–1000 ms or 23 tempo divisions, feedback (loop gain 1.5 × the knob, soft-limited), one-pole low / high cut in the loop |
| Orbit | ValhallaSpaceModulator | modulation machine: barber-pole rise and rise / fall, through-zero flange + / −, tri and octo choruses, doubler, drift variants, ensemble, symphonic; rate ±10 Hz, depth to 50 ms, manual offset, signed feedback, equal-power mix |
| Lattice Mod | ValhallaUberMod | multitap modulated delay: 1–16 taps spread over the delay, slope / skew / random, detune (slow random) and vibrato per tap with over-mod, rotating stereo feedback, modulated diffusion, drive with noise, low / high cut, dark colour, spatial crossover, width, half speed |

Measured and reproduced (details and residuals in the round's document): echo times and tempo sync to the sample,
the feedback laws (Echoform: loop gain = knob / 100 %; Spiral Echo: 1.5 × knob; Lattice: = knob), the mix laws
(equal power, Spiral Echo linear), each character's band limit, harmonics and noise, wow / flutter depth and rates,
the shifter / pitch amounts, Lattice's tap layout and gains. Not reproduced: the originals' exact diffusion, ducking
and "era" voicings, ValhallaDelay's "duck" variants' built-in ducking, UberMod's tempo-sync table.

Valhalla, ValhallaDelay, ValhallaFreqEcho, ValhallaSpaceModulator and ValhallaUberMod are trademarks of Valhalla DSP,
LLC; they are named only to say which plugin each LYNX effect is inspired by and stands in for. LYNX is not affiliated
with, endorsed or sponsored by Valhalla DSP.

|---|---|---|
| Facet EQ | surgical / mastering parametric EQs, e.g. FabFilter Pro-Q | 8 bands (bell, shelves, cuts 6–96 dB/oct, notch, band pass, tilt) on analog prototypes; its own editor with a live pre / post spectrum analyser, draggable nodes (double-click adds, wheel = Q, right-click = shape menu), band solo; per-band dynamic EQ (threshold and range, attack / release, detector on the input or a sidechain track); zero-latency, natural-phase (320 samples) and linear-phase (4608 samples) modes with the latency compensated by PDC |

## LYNX originals: dynamics

Three dynamics processors of LYNX's own design (REA round 108, [`docs/analise/REA_rodada108.md`](analise/REA_rodada108.md)),
in the roles of the style compressor, multiband dynamics and gate most mix engineers know. Unlike the mixing suite
above they were **fitted to measurements**: the official trial versions of the reference plugins were run only as a
DAW runs them (parameters set through the VST3 API, test tones in, audio out — [`MEASURE_fabfilter.md`](analise/MEASURE_fabfilter.md)),
never opened, disassembled or decompiled; the curves and timings below are our own models of what we measured, with
their residuals documented. Own names, own code, own panels (dark / red, live gain-reduction and level graphs). All
are on every mixer insert (*Insert*), report their latency before the first block and never allocate on the audio thread.

| LYNX engine | In the role of | What it is | Fit to the measurements |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crest Compressor | style compressors (FabFilter Pro-C 3) | 11 styles (Clean, Allround, Punch, Upward, Two-way, Vari-mu, Classic, Opto, Vocal, Bus, Pumping), threshold, ratio 1–100:1, knee 0–72 dB, range, attack, release (+ auto), hold, look-ahead with a maximum-look-ahead latency switch, 3-band side-chain EQ (Facet EQ shapes), side-chain level / external input / listen, stereo link, character (warm / crisp / bright, pre or post, drive), 2x–8x oversampling of the whole gain path, auto gain, mix, input / output | static curves within 1 dB of 84 measured points; 50 % attack / release within ~15 %; character harmonics within ~3 dB |
| Prism Multiband | multiband dynamics (FabFilter Pro-MB) | four bands (three crossovers, 12 / 24 / 48 dB/oct), each compress / expand, downward or upward by the sign of its range, threshold, ratio, knee, attack / release %, level, solo, on; look-ahead, mix, input / output; **transparent at rest** (a band without gain change leaves the signal untouched) | band compression within ~2 dB of the measured curve; expansion, upward expansion and timings in the measured ranges |
| Sentry Gate | gates / expanders (FabFilter Pro-G) | Classic, Clean, Vocal, Guitar and Upward styles, threshold, ratio 1–100:1 (expander to gate), range 0–100 dB, attack, release, hold, knee, look-ahead (10 ms latency when on), side-chain high / low pass, external side chain, listen, dry mix, output | expansion start points per style as measured; closing / opening times within ~35 % |

When a project uses one of these FabFilter plugins and it is not installed, the LYNX engine stands in for it **with
the plugin's saved settings translated** (Pro-C 3 → Crest, Pro-MB → Prism, Pro-G → Sentry, Saturn 2 → Ember's
multiband mode): the state layout was learned by saving the trial's state after each parameter change, nothing else.
The original plugin and its state are kept byte for byte, so the project opens with the real plugin wherever it is
installed. FabFilter, Pro-C, Pro-MB, Pro-G and Saturn are trademarks of FabFilter Software Instruments; they are named
only to say which role each LYNX effect plays. LYNX is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by FabFilter.

## LYNX originals: vocal pitch

| LYNX engine | In the role of | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| LYNX Tune | automatic vocal pitch correctors, e.g. Antares Auto-Tune, Waves Tune Real-Time | real-time pitch correction on every mixer insert (*Insert*): key and scale (13 scales + custom), per-note switches on a keyboard strip, retune speed (0 ms = the hard "robot" effect … 400 ms), humanize (lets held notes keep their vibrato), formant preserve and formant shift, transpose, A4 reference 430–450 Hz, voice range, low-latency mode (≈ 16 ms instead of ≈ 25 ms for alto / tenor), MIDI target notes (the notes held on a Channel Rack channel — played live or from a pattern — become the targets), mix; a live pitch display (detected note, cents and Hz, target note, correction meter, 8-second scrolling graph of the input and corrected pitch) |

LYNX Tune is LYNX's own design, written only from published DSP: YIN pitch detection (de Cheveigné & Kawahara, 2002)
and TD-PSOLA pitch shifting (Moulines & Charpentier, 1990), which keeps the formants in place. No third-party plugin was
opened, run or analysed to make it, and no preset, name, graphic or manual text of one is used
([`docs/analise/REA_rodada95.md`](analise/REA_rodada95.md)). Accuracy on synthetic vowels: within 3 cents of the target
note with instant retune; it never allocates on the audio thread and reports its latency to PDC. Antares and Auto-Tune
are trademarks of Antares Audio Technologies, Waves Tune of Waves Audio; they are named only to say which role LYNX Tune
plays. LYNX is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by them.
